name: Balanced score of retrieval on file, topic, orientation, no-context, memory, public-repository and grouping requests, with the index size and the cost of reading sources
purpose: An arm is judged by one number: whether what a request needs is among the units shown within a fixed token budget, in the right order, without noise tokens (an outdated fact counts as noise), nothing is shown when nothing is needed, and the arm does not read the sources at request time, at an index size, price and time a consumer would pay. The general methods of retrieval are measured, not one consumer's needs.
record: Per arm, the balanced score (accuracy, cost and time; [balance.context_retrieval]), one number per arm per stage. The case set mixes seven kinds with the weights of evaluation/context_retrieval/mix.py (63 file, 126 topic, 32 orientation, 32 none, 47 memory, 63 topic_open, 32 grouping): file-finding tasks, topic tasks taken from the git history (the files a commit changed are the needed ones; any learning uses only older commits), orientation, requests that need no context, long-term conversational memory (a pinned sample of LongMemEval, MIT: timestamped sessions, knowledge updates where a newer fact supersedes an older one, temporal and multi-session questions, unanswerable questions), the same topic tasks over three public BSD-3 repositories at pinned commits, and grouping tasks whose focus is a sibling repository so the needed files lie outside the request's focus. Items may carry metadata (kind, author role, timestamp, home groupings) and requests a time and a focus; an arm that ignores them is unchanged. Labels are graded (needed, helpful, irrelevant); a case's utility is 0.60 recall of the needed items within 4000 tokens, 0.25 nDCG@10 and 0.15 times one minus the noise share of the tokens shown; an index larger than the corpus gives up that share of every case. Reading the sources while answering is metered (source calls, records, megabytes) and charged to the case's cost at the prices of mix.py; building the store from the sources belongs to metric-cards-from-files, not to an arm. In the details: each kind's mean utility and counted cases, the memory question types, recall, nDCG, noise, units, index size, build seconds, and the source calls, cost, scan share and out-of-scope reads.
disadvantages: One chat-memory benchmark (English, one style, turns as items) and four Python repositories with commit-subject wording, not prose folders or a consumer's real requests; the mix is set by value and a sample of real requests should calibrate it; files and turns stand for relevance, so a needed passage inside a needed item is not told from the rest of it; the library's accuracy is a pass count, so fractional utility enters as a pass when it is above a fixed place per case (its expectation is the mean utility); a cold dense build is minutes and is not in the seconds per request; the source limits are vacuous on data whose items all lie in scope.
